Mangalore to Lakshadweep ship Ticket price 2025

Are you planning a dream vacation to India’s “Coral Paradise”? While most travelers fly from Kochi, the Mangalore to Lakshadweep ship journey is a hidden gem for budget travelers and sea lovers.

If you are searching for the Mangalore to Lakshadweep ship ticket price one way, the latest 2025 schedule, or the cheapest way to reach these islands, you have come to the right place.

In this detailed guide, we will break down the ship fare from Mangalore 2025, compare “Ticket vs. Package” costs, and give you a step-by-step blueprint to book your voyage safely.

Mangalore to Lakshadweep Ship Ticket Price 2025

Before we look at the prices, it is important to understand a crucial rule: Ticket prices depend on who you are.

  1. Islander Rates: Highly subsidized for locals.
  2. Tourist Rates: Higher, often sold as part of a package (like Silver Sand or Samudram).

Here is the breakdown of Mangalore to Lakshadweep ship ticket prices for tourists who want to book transportation only (requires a valid Entry Permit beforehand).

Mangalore to lakshadweep ship ticket price one way

Important: These are estimated base fares. If you do not have a pre-approved Lakshadweep Entry Permit and a confirmed hotel booking on the island, you cannot buy just a ticket. Most tourists from Mangalore prefer the Silver Sand Package for a hassle-free experience.

Lakshadweep Samudram & Silver Sand Package Price from Mangalore

For most tourists, the best way to travel is by booking a government-organized tour package. These packages include your ship ticket, entry permit, food, and island stay.

1. Silver Sand Package (The Mangalore Special)

This is the most popular option for travelers starting specifically from Mangalore or Beypore.

  • Route: Mangalore → Kalpeni Island → Mangalore
  • Duration: 2 Nights / 3 Days (or sometimes 1 Day excursion)
  • Price (Approx): ₹8,500 – ₹12,500 per person.
  • Inclusions: Ship fare (Bunk/Seat), meals on board, island sightseeing, and entry permit.

2. Lakshadweep Samudram Package Price from Mangalore

The famous Samudram Package is a 5-day cruise visiting Kavaratti, Kalpeni, and Minicoy.

  • Departure: Usually from Kochi, but sometimes schedules connect via Mangalore.
  • Cost (2025):
    • Adult: ₹35,000 – ₹45,000 (Diamond Class)
    • Child: ₹25,000 – ₹32,000
  • Accommodation: You sleep on the ship (MV Kavaratti) and visit islands during the day.

Ship from Mangalore to Kavaratti Price & Routes

If you have a friend/relative on the island or a confirmed resort booking at Kavaratti, you can book a direct ticket.

Route: Mangalore (New Mangalore Port) → Kavaratti

  • Distance: Approx 360 km
  • Ship from Mangalore to Kavaratti Price:
    • Bunk: ~₹3,000
    • Cabin: ~₹8,000+
  • Travel Time: 16 to 18 hours

Other Common Routes from Mangalore:

  • Mangalore to Kadmat: Popular for water sports lovers.
  • Mangalore to Amini: Mostly for locals and government officials.
  • Mangalore to Kalpeni: The main route for the Silver Sand package.

Mangalore to Lakshadweep Ship Schedule 2025

One of the most common questions is: “Does the ship run every day?”

The answer is NO.

Ships from Mangalore operate on a rotational schedule, usually once a week or bi-weekly during the fair season (October to May).

Pro Tip: The Mangalore Lakshadweep ship schedule 2025 is released month-by-month. Always check the officiallakport.utl.gov.inwebsite 15-20 days before your trip.

Mangalore to Lakshadweep Ship Travel Time

The journey is not short, but it is scenic. Here is how long you will be at sea:

  • Average Time: 14 to 18 hours
  • Fastest Ship: MV Kavaratti (approx 14-15 hours)
  • Slowest Ship: Smaller vessels or cargo-cum-passenger ships (up to 20 hours)

What impacts travel time?

  • Weather: Rough seas can delay the ship by 2-3 hours.
  • Stops: If the ship stops at another island (e.g., Amini) before your destination, the time increases.

Lakshadweep Ship Booking Online: Step-by-Step

Booking a ship ticket is slightly complex due to permit rules. Here is how to do Lakshadweep ship booking online safely:

Method 1: The “Hassle-Free” Package Route (Recommended)

  1. Visit the SPORTS (Lakshadweep Tourism) website.
  2. Select “Silver Sand Package” (for Mangalore departure).
  3. Choose your date and pay online.
  4. Benefit: The permit is arranged by them automatically.

Method 2: The “Do-It-Yourself” Ticket Route

  1. Get Permit: Apply for an e-Permit at epermit.utl.gov.in. You need a local sponsor or a confirmed hotel booking.
  2. Wait for Approval: This takes 7-15 days.
  3. Book Ticket: Once you have the permit, create an account on lakport.utl.gov.in.
  4. Select Seat: Look for “Mangalore” as the source port.
  5. Payment: Pay via Net Banking/UPI.

Quick Tip: Online tickets sell out in minutes after the schedule is published. Be ready at 10:00 AM or 11:00 AM on the opening day

Cheapest Way to Reach Lakshadweep from Mangalore

If you are a student or budget traveler asking for the absolute cheapest way to reach Lakshadweep from Mangalore, here is the hack:

  1. Avoid Flights: Flights from Kochi to Agatti cost ₹5,000 – ₹10,000 one way. Ships are 50% cheaper.
  2. Choose Bunk Class: The Bunk class ticket is approx ₹2,500.
  3. Go in a Group: Sharing accommodation on the island reduces costs.
  4. Use Government Huts: Stay in government tourist huts instead of private luxury resorts.
  5. Avoid December: Prices for packages hike by 10-15% in December (peak season). Travel in October or February for the best rates.

Facilities on Board: What to Expect?

When you pay the Mangalore to Lakshadweep ship ticket price, what do you actually get?

  • Sleeping: Clean bunks with bedsheets and pillows (in AC dorms).
  • Food: Breakfast, Lunch, and Dinner are served in the cafeteria. It is simple, spicy, and tasty (mostly Kerala style).
  • Medical: A small dispensary with a doctor is available for seasickness.
  • Prayer Room: Most ships have a prayer area.
  • Entertainment: No WiFi! But you get endless views of the deep blue Arabian Sea and flying fish.

FAQ For Mangalore to Lakshadweep ship Ticket price 2025

Here are the answers to the specific questions users are asking on Google right now:

1. What is the ship fare from Mangalore to Lakshadweep 2025 for tourists?

For a standard Bunk Class ticket, expect to pay between ₹2,500 and ₹3,500. If you choose the Silver Sand Package (inclusive of permit/food), it costs around ₹8,500.

2. Can I book a one-way ticket from Mangalore?

Yes, but only if you have a valid Entry Permit or a Clearance Certificate from the island administration. You cannot board the ship without it.

3. Which is the best ship from Mangalore?

MV Kavaratti is the best in terms of comfort and stability. MV Lakshadweep Sea is also a good option for shorter journeys.

4. How long does the Mangalore to Lakshadweep ship take?

It takes approximately 16 hours. You typically board in the evening (around 5 PM) and reach the island the next morning (around 9 AM).

5. Is the Samudram Package available from Mangalore?

Usually, the Samudram package starts from Kochi. However, you should check with SPORTS if they have a scheduled pickup from Mangalore for specific dates in 2025.

title: Mangalore to Lakshadweep Ship Ticket Price
primaryKeyword: mangalore to lakshadweep ship ticket price
contentHtml:
Mangalore is one of the few mainland ports with a passenger ship to Lakshadweep, so it is a genuine alternative to sailing from Kochi. The service is run by the Lakshadweep administration, fares are fixed by class rather than invented by travel sites, and you need an entry permit before you board. Here is how the route actually works, what a ticket involves, and how to book it.

Is there a ship from Mangalore to Lakshadweep?

Yes. A government passenger vessel sails from the Old Mangalore Port at Bunder to Lakshadweep, with MV Minicoy the ship most associated with this route, typically serving Kadmat island. The ship carries around 150 passengers, and the service is operated by the Lakshadweep administration, not by private agents. It runs on a set schedule rather than daily, and sailings depend on the season and sea conditions.

Mangalore to Lakshadweep distance and travel time

Lakshadweep lies roughly 144 nautical miles off Mangalore, and the crossing takes in the region of 14 hours, so it is an overnight sea journey. Exact timing varies with the weather and the ship, so confirm the sailing time when you book.

Mangalore to Lakshadweep ship ticket price

Fares on the government ships are set by the Lakshadweep administration by class, the same system used on the Kochi route. A basic second-class seat is the cheapest way across, first-class and premium cabins cost more for a berth on the overnight leg, and children, infants and islanders are charged at different rates. Prices are revised from time to time, so the administration's counter is the only reliable source for the current fare; be wary of sites quoting exact rupee figures for named ships, as those are often out of date or made up.

As a rough idea of the scale, second-class seats on the comparable Kochi to Lakshadweep ships start at a few thousand rupees, with cabins costing more. Use that only as a guide and confirm the Mangalore fare at the ticket counter before you pay.

You need an entry permit for Lakshadweep

Lakshadweep is a protected island group, and every non-resident visitor needs an entry permit before boarding, regardless of which port they sail from. You apply through the Lakshadweep administration, usually with a passport-size photo, valid ID proof and a police clearance certificate, then carry the approved permit with your ticket. Apply well ahead of your date, because you cannot board without it.

How to book Mangalore to Lakshadweep ship tickets

Tickets are issued by the Lakshadweep administration through its port office. In Mangalore the ticketing counter is at the Old Mangalore Port area at Bunder; you can also book through the administration's reservation system where it is available online. Seats are limited on a 150-passenger ship and fill up in peak season, so book as early as you can and keep printed copies of both your ticket and permit.

Best time to sail

Seas are calmest and sailings most reliable from around October to May. During the southwest monsoon, roughly June to September, the sea off the Karnataka coast is rough and services are often reduced or suspended, so avoid planning a monsoon crossing.

Quick tips before you go

  • Arrange your permit and ticket together, and carry printed copies of both.
  • Choose a cabin for the overnight leg if you are prone to seasickness.
  • Carry cash, as card facilities on the islands can be limited.
  • Pack sunscreen, a light jacket for the deck, and motion-sickness tablets.

Comparing routes? See our guides on the Kochi to Lakshadweep ship ticket price and the Cordelia cruise from Mumbai to Lakshadweep.

Frequently asked questions

Is there a direct ship from Mangalore to Lakshadweep?

Yes. A government passenger ship, commonly MV Minicoy, sails from the Old Mangalore Port at Bunder to Lakshadweep, usually serving Kadmat island, on a scheduled basis.

How long does the Mangalore to Lakshadweep ship take?

The crossing is roughly 144 nautical miles and takes around 14 hours, so it is an overnight journey. Confirm the exact timing when you book.

What is the Mangalore to Lakshadweep ship ticket price?

Fares are fixed by class by the Lakshadweep administration, with a second-class seat the cheapest and cabins costing more. Prices are revised periodically, so confirm the current fare at the port ticket counter rather than relying on figures quoted online.

Do I need a permit to visit Lakshadweep from Mangalore?

Yes. Every non-resident visitor needs an entry permit from the Lakshadweep administration before boarding, whichever port they sail from. Apply well in advance and carry it with your ticket.

Where do I book the Mangalore to Lakshadweep ferry?

Book through the Lakshadweep administration's ticket counter at the Old Mangalore Port at Bunder, or its online reservation system where available. Avoid private sites that promise instant tickets at fixed prices.
